dedupe_keys.name: simpy and streamlit tutorial models for open health service delivery discrete event simulation

description: These tutorial materials teach health service researchers to build open discrete-event simulation models of health service delivery with the Python library SimPy and to share them as interactive web apps with Streamlit. The worked examples model patients arriving at a service, queuing for staff, cubicles or beds and being treated, and report waiting times and resource use across replications, so that NHS partners can run what-if experiments in a browser without installing code. The provider is Thomas Monks and Alison Harper, who describe the approach in NIHR Open Research (2023, volume 3, article 48). Coverage is generic: the examples are stylised NHS services, not a calibrated hospital. The code is on GitHub under the MIT licence with an archived release on Zenodo, runs in Python 3.10 or newer through a conda environment or Binder, and the latest tag read today is v2.0.0. Caveats: the models are teaching examples with illustrative parameters, and users must supply local arrival and service data before drawing conclusions. Simulation uses: a template for emergency department, ward or clinic capacity models, and for testing surge scenarios such as a sudden rise in arrivals after an incident. Related records: the NHS ambulance discrete-event model (model-ambulance-des-nhsx) is a similar open SimPy model, and Synthea (model-synthea) can supply synthetic demand.
